lines: * [FEATURE] Ingester: Add the experimental `-ingester.partition-ring.create-partitions-with-derived-tokens` and `-ingester.partition-ring.max-derived-token-partitions` flags, allowing ingesters to create partitions with tokens derived from the partition ID instead of storing them in the partition ring, which reduces the size of the memberlist state. Before you enable `-ingester.partition-ring.create-partitions-with-derived-tokens` on the ingesters, ensure that `-ingester.partition-ring.max-derived-token-partitions` is applied to all partition ring readers and ingesters, with a value higher than the highest partition ID. Partition IDs at or above the maximum are rejected, and readers that don't have the maximum yet fail when an ingester creates a partition with derived tokens. #16763

* [FEATURE] Mimirtool: Add the experimental `--partition.derived-tokens` flag to `mimirtool partition-ring add-partition` to add partitions with tokens derived from the partition ID instead of stored in the ring. #16763

* [FEATURE] Ingester, Block-builder: Add the experimental `-blocks-storage.tsdb.histogram-chunk-encoding` flag (per-tenant `histogram_chunk_encoding` limit) to select the encoding used for new native histogram chunks (`histogram` or `histogram_st`). `histogram_st` selects the start-timestamp-capable encodings for both integer and float histogram chunks. The overrides-exporter can export it as a numeric value (`5` for `histogram`, `8` for `histogram_st`) when `histogram_chunk_encoding` is added to `-overrides-exporter.enabled-metrics`. #16705

+* [FEATURE] Query-frontend: Add the experimental `-query-frontend.cardinality-estimation-cache.*` flags to store cardinality estimates in a dedicated memcached cache instead of the results cache. Disabled by default. #17173
* [ENHANCEMENT] API: OTLP translation headers (`-api.otlp-translation-headers-enabled`) are now stable and no longer experimental. The flag remains disabled by default. #17076
* [ENHANCEMENT] Store-gateway: Emit exponential native histograms for `cortex_bucket_stores_blocks_sync_seconds` alongside existing classic buckets. #17077
* [ENHANCEMENT] Reduce partition shuffle-shard construction cost after ring updates by reusing immutable token indexes. #17012
* [CHANGE] Remove configuration to disable use of the bucket-index since it has been mandatory since version 2.11. #16980
* [FEATURE] Enable active query tracking in read path components to keep track of running queries during crashes. #16876 #16981
* [FEATURE] Allow common (`mimirComponentAnnotations`) and per-component annotations (`<component>_annotations`) to be set on each Mimir component. #17143
+* [FEATURE] Add the optional `memcached-cardinality` cache for query-frontend cardinality estimates. Set `cache_cardinality_enabled: true` to deploy it. Requires `cache_frontend_enabled`. #17173

* [ENHANCEMENT] Add `multi_zone_ingester_zpdb_cross_zone_eviction_delay` config option to set `crossZoneEvictionDelay` on the ingester `ZoneAwarePodDisruptionBudget`. Defaults to `20m` when `ingest_storage_enabled` is true, and to unset otherwise. #16271
* [ENHANCEMENT] Compactor: Allow the drain autoscaler's speed estimates to be read from recording rules. #16283
* [ENHANCEMENT] Updated rollout-operator jsonnet library to v0.39.0. #16440

@@ -156,11 +156,13 @@ Queries that return few or no series should be executed with fewer or no shards

When determining the number of shards to use for a given query, the sharding logic can optionally take into account the cardinality (number of series) observed during previous executions of the same query for similar time ranges.

To enable this feature, set `-query-frontend.query-sharding-target-series-per-shard` to a value representing roughly how many series each shard should fetch, and configure the results cache via the `query-frontend.results-cache.*` flags.
-This is necessary even when results caching is disabled, as the estimates are stored in the same cache that's used for query result caching.
+This is necessary even when results caching is disabled, as by default the estimates are stored in the same cache that's used for query result caching.
The value that you set for this flag is one of several parameters that the sharding logic uses to determine the appropriate number of shards for a query.
Therefore, it will not strictly be complied with in all cases, and the actual number of series fetched per shard might exceed the limit.
This is likely to happen in cases where the cardinality of a query changes rapidly within a short period of time.
+You can store the estimates in an optional dedicated cache with the `-query-frontend.cardinality-estimation-cache.*` flags, but the results cache is still required.
Estimates for query cardinality are only ever used to reduce the number of shards compared to the case when cardinality estimation is disabled.

Other parameters that limit the total number of shards, such as `-query-frontend.query-sharding-total-shards`, will still provide an upper bound for the number of shards even when cardinality estimation is enabled and would suggest the use of a higher number of shards.
